verdict.tagline: Charming slime farming expands into a sprawling exploration adventure.
for_you_if: you enjoy collecting and farming cute creatures
you want an open world with hidden secrets to discover
you need a game that runs well on modest hardware
not_for_you_if: you dislike tight inventory limits and early money grinds
you are bothered by map bugs and falling through the ground
you want to avoid endless ranch maintenance tasks

Its pretty simple to graphs', play this if you just want chill experience i guess. Pretty old tho

Slime Rancher is a game that looked me directly in the eyes and said this is not for you and I respected the honesty, but for some reason still bought it - thanks steam sale!

Monomi Park built what is genuinely a well made, cheerful, mechanically solid farming sim where you vacuum up adorable bouncy creatures, put them in pens, feed them, and harvest their deposits. That sentence should tell you everything you need to know about whether this is your game or not. If reading that made you smile it's probably a great time. If you just stared at the screen for a second that's also valid and we can move on together.

The game commits completely to its vibe and there's something admirable about that. It's colorful, it's stress free, it has zero interest in making you feel bad about anything, and the world has a gentle charm to it that a certain kind of person finds deeply comforting. That person is not a man in his thirties who came up gaming on Doom and GTA.

The humor is genuinely there in small doses and the farming loop is competent enough that you can see why it found its audience. It just found a very specific audience and if you don't recognize yourself in the description of someone who wants to spend an afternoon collecting wobbly pink spheres and sorting them by type then this one was never going to land.

No shame in knowing your demographic. Works fine on Steam Deck and PC if you need to find out the hard way like the rest of us.

cohorts.summary: Players feed slimes, manage a ranch, and gather droppings to sell in the market.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the gameplay loop involves feeding slimes, managing a ranch, and gathering their droppings to sell in a market.

citations.review_text: In this game, I can run around and complete chores, make sure everyone's fed, pick up poop, wrangle the chickens and squishies, go to bed to sleep for what seems like two seconds; only to start all over the next day. Like real life, but without all of the dirty dishes. 10/10!
kidnap slime -> feed slime -> collect slime poop -> sell slime poop in a mysterious market -> make money

If you like collecting, feeding, and selling the droppings of funny little blob critters, this game is for you. Easy to get the hang of, fun to do. I do recommend making more farms for food than you think you need, the little guys love to eat and start to get rebellious if you run out of food.

cohorts.label: 20-100h
cohorts.summary: The experience features limited inventory space and manual maintenance demands, balanced by smooth optimization for simpler systems.

claims.claim: The game's early hours involve a tedious grind for money and limited inventory space, forcing constant trips back to the home base.

citations.review_text:
While I enjoyed the later stages of Slime Rancher, the first 5-10 hours felt like a grinding slog. That, plus some frustrating gameplay choices, make me not want to recommend the game.

I love exploration games, but exploring in Slime Rancher is severely limited at first. You need money to open up new areas and buy upgrades to survive the attacking slimes, which is tedious with the starter slimes. Then once you go exploring, you have to return home all the time because your extremely limited inventory (just 4 types of items!) is full with new items you want to safely take home. Which involves a lot of walking back and forth because you don't have resources for teleporters yet.

Once you get more money and automate the ranch chores, the game gets fun and quite addictive. It's just a shame it takes so long to get there.

At first the game is super relaxing and exploring is fun, but later the tiny inventory completely ruins the pace forcing you to constantly run back and forth and the grind at the end gets really boring. Still, it's worth recommending just for the great initial experience.

claims.claim: Late-game automation requires ongoing manual maintenance, such as sprinkling water to recharge automated workers.

citations.review_text:
[h1]Just Some Fun, Slime [strike]Slavery[/strike] Chaos[/h1]

[h2]The Good[/h2]
[list]
    [*]Artstyle is obviously the first striking point of the game, (most) areas are visually calm and friendly, and the slimes themselves are incredibly cute and visually appealing, even when they're angy
    [*]Ranching the slimes are pretty fun, chaotic, yet free. You can choose any slimes, and there's no restrictions for the most part for where and what slimes you decide to ranch, tho there are different profits
    [*]I really love the slime merging mechanic, adds a surprising amount of customization to slime ranching
    [*]The game has certain dangers and antagonizing forces, but they aren't overly difficult to overcome or frustrating. Instead they add a bit of fun pushback to the game
[/list]

[h2]The Bad[/h2]
[list]
    [*]The process of the [spoiler]Science Lab[/spoiler] is a bit tedious imo, both harvesting resources for and using [spoiler]gadgets[/spoiler]. And then outcome of [spoiler]automation[/spoiler] also kinda defeats the chaotic ranching vibe of the game a lil
    [*]The side areas where you do [spoiler]unique missions with unique slimes[/spoiler] are fun for the first time, but a bit boring to grind
[/list]

[h2]The Random[/h2]
[list]
    [*]Gluttonous fcks
    [*]BEEG GLUTTONOUS FCKS
    [*]I appreciate that there is a story, but it was kinda insignificant
[/list]

[h2]Overall Thoughts[/h2]
Fun lil ranching game where you mess around with lil blobby guys. You WILL get attached to these dumb blobs, you have no choice

Game is very grindy and even the automation you receive almost at the end of the plot is annoying - yeah, you get automation but now you have to go all over the farm and sprinkle water to recharge automated workers. Also there is a limit of automation for each location. Even with teleporters around the ranch it got very tedious.

Going for all achievements is another matter as it got quite frustrating as some of the game mechanics started to get tiresome while going for the timed mode achievements. claims.claim: The game is well-optimized for lower-powered systems.

citations.review_text: Banger of a game. Super under-rated farming game. Plays pretty well on lower power systems.

Pretty good, there's really not many substantive complaints you can make about a game like this when its done as well as Slime Rancher is. I remember when this game was just starting to be a thing in it's early access day and the wealth of content you have for it now is genuinely impressive, you can tell the dev team had a lot of care and good will towards their community for supporting them and believing in their project as hard as they have.

Not something I would personally play endless hours but there is certainly a fair amount of more focused late game grinding / micro easements to get up to if you're the type. Pick a lazy weekend and have some fun with Slime Rancher, not a bad choice at all! (It's also extremely extremely well optimized as a plus for those with smaller builds/laptops).
its a perfect game for a low resources pc, recomended for casual players. 9/10

This is how a game should be made, fun game-play and well optimized.
They don't make them like this anymore.
10/10

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the exploration as wide open with virtually no invisible walls, allowing players to discover hidden secrets and rewards across the map.

citations.review_text:
What is there to say about your favourite game of all time?

Being the first video game I ever played, this magnificent experience has been with me almost all my life. And what a companion to have! I likely wouldn't be alive If it didn't exsist. The ammount of comfort this game has brought me during difficult times and the ammount of happiness it has brought be during the good times can only be compared to the ammount spending time with my closest friends, family and cats have brought, and that should say a lot. This game is best compared to a warm hug. Everything is cute, cozy and comforting, while still being a really fun and exciting game! 

Gameplay wise, Slime Rancher is incredible. Being focused on exploration at it's core, the game features an expansive open-world with almost no invisible walls! There are many many secrets and no place is too hidden, so your curiosity is always rewarded and you'll always have something to bring back, be that new slimes, resources, or maybe a fun new toy for the slimes you already have! The movement isn't the smoothest, but it has its' own charm and is easy to get used to. In general most mechanics can be described the same way, "a bit clunky, but simple and easy to get used to, with its' own charm"

In terms of visuals, the game is fine. the textures can be a little odd, and many areas are quite empty. In other words, it's sub-par, at least by modern standards, but you don't really notice, especially with so many slimes jumping around! The game is also super visually consistent, so once you're immersed, you wont be taken out of it. You can also do a lot of decorating, so even if you dislike an area, it's easy to make it your own. 

The game's story is simple and mostly in the background, but it does its' job really well. It's very heartfelt and a nice break from the stress of ranching! And man, THE ENDINGS! they will stick with you! they're neither grand, nor heartwrenching, but they are perfect for Slime Rancher! Eve…

This game makes me feel a touch conflicted. For the most part, this game is an extremely cute "cozy," farm sim game. Exploring the world feels very fun, and I was always pleasantly surprised to find little secrets and rewards around every corner. The actual ranching part is fun to, I loved expanding and upgrading my farm. The slimes are extremely cute as well. 

Where this game starts to fall off for me is the gameplay loop of ranching. There are at least a dozen different slimes that all have different needs, but most of those needs can be dealt with either with an upgrade to their pen or just keeping them well fed. For the few have challenges that could effect other slimes, the ranch is big enough that you could keep them pretty separated from the others. At the beginning of the game, managing the ranch is great, but as you grow the number of slimes you keep, it begins to be an endless cycle of maintenance. There was always slimes to feed, or food to harvest, or plorts to sell. Once you get deeper into the endgame, you can add some automation to the farm, but I was left wishing I could fully (or nearly fully) automate my ranch.

Overall the game is great, and many people, including myself sometimes, love a game where you have infinite tasks to check off. I had a great time with this game, but likely will not be replaying it or spending much more time with it after getting all the achievements.

Slime Rancher was such a fun and relaxing game to play on PC. I was drawn in right away by the cute art style and colorful world. It’s one of those games that’s easy to pick up and play when you want something lighthearted and stress-free.

My favorite part was exploring and unlocking new areas. Every time I opened a new section of the map, I felt excited to see what new slimes, resources, or secrets I would find. Collecting slimes was surprisingly addictive, and I especially enjoyed combining different slimes together to create hybrids. It was always fun to see what the new combinations would look like and how they would behave.

The game does a great job of balancing exploration, collecting, and managing your ranch without making anything feel too complicated. There was always something to work toward, whether it was upgrading my ranch, finding new slimes, or discovering a new area.

Overall, Slime Rancher is a charming game that kept me entertained for hours. If you enjoy exploration, collecting cute creatures, and relaxing gameplay, I would definitely recommend giving it a try.

Cute and joyful, this game is great.

In summary: 10/10, just buy it.
It is repeatable, does not get boring, has a good amount of content (including end-game), has nice mechanics, and the progression is consistent and controllable.

After a hundred hours, the game is still interesting, re-doing it is as fun as improving existing saves.

[hr][/hr]

The game loop is fun and "simple done well":
 1. Collect new slimes
 2. Farm / Plant / Feed
 3. Improve farm / upgrade things / build gadgets
 4. Discover new places
 5. Restart loop

The progress is consistent and in the right speed (for some things - such as gadgets - it ends to the slow side).
The speed in which new slimes and items appear can be controlled by you, which is a great feature. You can take your time to reestructure the ranch after every new slime, or just speedrun it all.

If you have a thing for organization or resource management, you can definitely have fun optimizing item placement in the ranch. There is just the perfect amount of variables to match for an amazing optimization/organization experience (slimes, food, chickens, gadgets, water sources).

End-game content is also very nice, and requires quite a bit of backstory recovery to pick - though it takes some time (it is kinda hidden, you have to either search the map carefully, or check guides online).

The only bug I could see was an overlap between a wall and the floating decoration chimes, that could be easily handled by vacuuming back the decoration. So, I'd say no problem with bugs, at all.

I was browsing STEAM.COM today when I found this great game - Slime Rancher. So I open it up, expecting to do some great Slime Ranching, but what do I find but an empty landscape without a slime in site- before realizing that the unpalatable pink blobls were meant to be the ranchable slimes that we were promised. I proceeded to cry for one day and one night, cursing the world for allowing a developer to catfish my slimey expectations like this, and for not capturing the true essence of the beautiful slime. The amorphous unpredictability of the body, morphing into a hungry mouth, one that eventually consumes plorts to evolve into the ever bigger largo, able to grow anywhere, and of course, being a local nuisance anywhere that it may choose to populate, but instead of the gorgeous curves, I was meant with a spherical sham, a rigid imitation that pales in comparison to any slime that I have ever laid my eyes upon. You have not truly made a game about slimes- you've made a mockery of a perfect enemy.

9/10 game I found the lack of proper collision detection funny
